source: Normal melting, boiling and decomposition points at 101 325 Pa of the catalogue molecules the critical-point table lacks, in kelvin (sources in degrees Celsius converted by adding 273.15): the CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics (editions as quoted by PubChem from HSDB), the NIST Chemistry WebBook (SRD 69, averaged phase-change values), the Merck Index, Hawley's Condensed Chemical Dictionary and the PhysProp database as quoted by PubChem, and English Wikipedia chemboxes where none of these gives a value; each entry names its own source. A substance that sublimes at 1 atm has its sublimation point as the boiling temperature and its triple point as the melting temperature, as carbon dioxide in critical-points.json; amino acids and nucleobases, whose quoted melting points are melting with decomposition, are stored as decomposition points; null where the source gives no value at 1 atm. Borane, nitrous, sulfurous, carbonic, hypochlorous and thiocyanic acid and sodium hypochlorite exist only in the gas phase, in solution or as hydrates, and krypton difluoride has no quoted point, so they are left out
